transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Recording: Yes (auto)
Attendees: Jordan Mitchell (Redwood AE), Priya Narang (Redwood SE), Samir Lowe (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (Cumulus Head of MLOps), Marc Reyes (VP Eng), Lena Ortiz (Cloud Security), Ben Yu (Platform Eng), Rita Alvarez (Product)

Summary (auto):
High-level Q4 health review focused on adoption barriers, burst/p95 latency incidents in Nov, cost run-rate, and next steps to pilot Dedicated capacity for peak inference. Customer asked for security artifacts and a short burn-in test to validate p99 under realistic load. Action items assigned for pricing, test harness, and sample traces.

Topics: usage trends, incident review, cost drivers, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, pilot plan, security artifacts, timeline and success criteria.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we can get started. Samir, you want to do quick intros?
[00:08] Samir: Yeah, quick one. I'm Samir, CSM on this account. We've been looking at the late October spike and the Nov 9th degradation; goal for today is to align on mitigation and pilot steps.
[00:18] Aisha: Thanks. From Cumulus side, I'm Aisha — running MLOps — Marc's on for infra questions, Lena is security, Ben for logs and traces, Rita for product adoption notes.
[00:28] Jordan: Perfect. Priya will run through some findings from our infra readout and then we'll talk options.
[00:35] Priya: Cool. I'll share my screen... uh (screen noise). Okay, so two quick bullets: first, usage has grown 4x since July, but the distribution is spiky — weekends heavy for certain flows — and second, p95 latency was fine, but we've seen p99 jumps during concurrent shopping funnels, spikes correlated with session replays.
[01:05] Marc: Can you quantify the p99? We saw some user-facing timeouts on Nov 9th.
[01:09] Priya: Yes, on average baseline p99 for the text gen route is ~920ms on hosted, but during the Nov 9th window it hit 2.4s at peak for about 18 minutes. There were also retry storms from your client side which amplified request concurrency.
[01:27] Ben: We did have retries; our SDK had an aggressive retry backoff that was misconfigured. That's on us. But curious — would Dedicated have handled that behavior differently?
[01:37] Jordan: Good question. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and a predictable max throughput; it would have avoided the capacity fall-through we saw, and also let you control batch sizing and eviction policies. But it's not a silver bullet — you still need client-side throttles.
[01:50] Aisha: Right, cost is our big worry. We've been bumped to 3x monthly run-rate — can you walk through where the spikes are coming from in billing?
[01:58] Priya: Sure. Three drivers: 1) increased request volume (obvious), 2) repeated short requests that defeat batching which increase per-token overhead, and 3) multiple model variants— you have dev vs prod pinned separately which fragments caching/KV hit rate. We showed a small model rationalization in the deck — quantization and a unified prod model would drop unit cost by ~25% in our estimates.
[02:26] Marc: For the quantization recommendation, we need to see impact on latency as well as output fidelity — recall retail search needs tight recall for SKU matches.
[02:35] Priya: Understood. We'll run a small eval with your trace to show quality delta. It should be minimal for rerank and search rank but we'll confirm.
[02:43] Rita: From product: adoption is stalling in a couple of teams because they keep hitting rate limits on nightly indexing jobs. We hit those around midnight and they get retried throughout the day.
[02:53] Jordan: Okay, that's a classic candidate for off-peak batch windows and pre-warming caches; Dedicated plus scheduled batch workers would help. Also we can set up a burst policy so day jobs don't displace interactive traffic.
[03:04] Lena: Security quick note — we need SOC2 type II evidence and a network diagram showing egress flows. Also any custodian controls for KMS/HSM if we move to Private or Dedicated in VPC.
[03:14] Samir: We'll attach SOC2 report and the architecture diagram. Jordan, Priya — can you collect what Lena needs?
[03:21] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll include SOC2, network diagram with ports, and the KMS integration doc.
[03:26] Marc: We also want to run a capacity burn-in sim. Can Redwood provide a 48 hour stress test harness that emulates our traffic distribution?
[03:33] Priya: Yes — we have a test harness and scripts. We'll need anonymized traces to replay realistic session distributions. Once we have those, we can provision a Dedicated pool in our staging region and run the 48-hour burn. That will show p95/p99 behavior and highlight tail latencies.
[03:48] Ben: How intrusive is the burn-in? We can't have it affect production.
[03:52] Priya: It runs against staging or a pinned Dedicated pool; it won't touch prod unless you give us credentials. We'll confine it to an isolated namespace.
[03:59] Aisha: Timeline — if we start pilot in Dec, we'd like to be live for holiday season. What's realistic?
[04:05] Jordan: If we get signatures for a small Dedicated pilot by Nov 30 and traces by Nov 24, we can run tests in first two weeks of Dec and aim to flip traffic gradationally before the holiday window.
[04:15] Marc: What's the minimum commitment for Dedicated trial? We need numbers to pitch to finance.
[04:20] Jordan: For pilots we offer a 90-day trial pricing model with a reduced commitment level — think of it as reserved baseline plus burst credits. I'll send a 3-tier pricing sheet that shows monthly equivalents for 6/12/24 month commitments.
[04:33] Rita: And SLA? We need p99 SLOs for critical routes.
[04:37] Priya: Our Dedicated SLO for interactive gen is p99 < 1.5s for the recommended capacity profiles; the holiday plan will combine auto-scale and pre-warmed instances to meet that. For hosted, the SLO is best-effort but we provide latency tiers in the dashboard.
[04:51] Lena: For compliance, if we go Dedicated in our VPC, what controls do we get? Auditable logs? KMS key ownership?
[04:58] Jordan: Dedicated in VPC gives you customer-managed KMS and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via secure log streaming. We also support SAML SSO and RBAC policy sync. We'll include sample log schema.
[05:09] Aisha: Let's flag the recurring incidents — we had 3 P1s in last quarter tied to capacity handoffs. How do you recommend preventing recurrence?
[05:16] Priya: Two-prong: stopgap is to add circuit-breaker and token-level quotas to limit client retries; medium term is Dedicated with capacity guardrails plus smarter batching and prefix caching for common prompts. We'll also set up alerting on KV miss rates and queue depth.
[05:32] Ben: We can add client-side backoff quickly. Actionable.
[05:35] Marc: One more — model rollout strategy. We can’t afford regressions during holidays. How to do controlled rollouts?
[05:42] Jordan: Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts at the route level. For holidays we'd recommend a phased rollout with automatic rollback on quality/regression triggers tied to your evaluation prompts. We'll pair that with traffic shadowing for full-scale validation.
[05:55] Rita: What's the data retention policy for logs used in evals? We have to keep PII out.
[05:59] Samir: We can mask or hash any PII — and for traces you can send sanitized samples. We'll sign an NDA amendment if you want explicit guarantees.
[06:09] Aisha: Okay let's recap next steps quickly. Jordan?
[06:12] Jordan: Recap: 1) I'll send Dedicated pricing and 3-tier commitment models by Nov 20. 2) Priya will share test harness, burn-in checklist, and sample scripts by Nov 19. 3) Samir will upload SOC2 and network diagram links by Nov 22. 4) Cumulus to provide anonymized traces by Nov 24. 5) We'll schedule 48-hour burn-in the week of Nov 29. 6) Pilot SOW draft from Samir by Nov 22.
[06:33] Lena: Sounds good. One ask: include the network port list and egress endpoints in the network diagram — security will need to pre-approve.
[06:40] Jordan: Noted, will include that.
[06:42] Marc: Any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:44] Ben: I think the only blocker is our ability to quickly sanitize traces — we'll prioritize it.
[06:49] Rita: Product wants a short playbook for when we hit tail latency — steps to triage so support can act quickly.
[06:54] Samir: We'll draft a 1-pager playbook and share by Nov 21.
[06:59] Jordan: Great. Appreciate everyone's time. We'll follow up with a meeting invite for the burn-in prep and the SOW doc.
[07:05] Aisha: Thanks, talk soon.

End of recording.
